newsitem.title: USA: Texaco sees Shell letter of intent by Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Texaco sees Shell letter of intent by Q1 '97.

text.p: Texaco Inc, outlining optimistic forecasts on its proposed U.S. downstream merger with Shell, expects to sign a letter of intent on the deal in the 1997 first quarter, Texaco's top executive said.
"(It should happen) not later than the first quarter of 1997," Chief Executive Peter Bijur told executives attending the annual analyst meeting at Texaco's headquarters here.

Phillip Carroll, president of Shell Oil Co, the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, meanwhile said in November he hoped the entire deal could be concluded by the end of 1997, but that many crucial items were still unresolved.
The proposed Texaco-Shell merger of U.S. refining and marketing operations also includes Star Enterprises, Texaco's joint venture with state-owned Saudi Aramco.
Bijur noted the merger will offer solid growth potential for both companies, as well as cost savings "higher than the level of the Mobil-BP merger," Bijur said.
Although he did not elaborate, he was referring to a similar donwstream merger of European refining and marketing assets by U.S. major Mobil Corp and British Petroleum Co Plc earlier this year.
